items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748053/a424f0c7a25f7be908a4e35181ae82ff2e28ad09.png"]
With the end of 2026 approaching, and major updates for both Hell Let Loose: Vietnam and Hell Let Loose on the horizon, we wanted to share news on the scheduled releases for both games.
Following a severe team17 network outage, we are now having to alter our upcoming release schedule.

We’re sorry to say that the release dates for Updates 2.0 and 3.0 have been pushed back as a result of the team17 infrastructure issues. Team17’s technical teams have been working to resolve the problem as quickly as possible so that Expression Games can continue delivering the upcoming content planned for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam.

Whilst this work continues, the development team has used the time to expand upon planned content. This includes an even bigger Update 2.0, featuring the brand-new Khe Sanh map, seven new weapons, additions to the US & Allied Forces, including the ANZAC Forces and Green Berets, and much more, including new free unlockable content.
Take a look at our updated Roadmap below to see what’s coming when Update 2.0 arrives in early December.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748053/048c6e7c46b5059e96d9adbb03f510e4f4a77146.jpg"]
Update 3.0 will follow in early 2027, bringing our next map, Rung Sat, armored personnel carriers (APCs), additional weapons and more.
We know this will be disappointing news for the Hell Let Loose: Vietnam community, and we greatly appreciate your patience and understanding.
In the meantime, get ready for the Khe Sanh Deep Dive video, coming tomorrow on the Hell Let Loose YouTube.[dynamiclink href="https://youtu.be/8oMD1H5cmG0"]
We’ll share confirmed release dates for both updates as soon as we’re in a position to do so.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748053/7ffe5709c0b9962f742069b6f1fd1ce2455f039c.png"]

We’re also sorry to share that Hell Let Loose has been affected by these issues. After assessing their impact, we’ve had to revisit our original content plans for Update 22. The focus is now on delivering our newest map, Lake Balaton, in early December.

For those already getting ready for the winter break, Lake Balaton and its frozen landscape will soon be drawing you back into the action. Take a first look at the newest map coming to Hell Let Loose below.[dynamiclink href="https://youtu.be/LdyQKvYFooM"]

The content deferred as part of these changes remains in active development as we continue developing and refining these upcoming additions, including new vehicles. We’re currently aiming to bring this content to players in early 2027.
We look forward to sharing more details about these additions, alongside our wider plans for the year ahead, early next year.
In the meantime, thank you for your continued support and understanding as we work to keep pushing both Hell Let Loose games forward.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748053/de3fb9d7f3a485d6132614b9dcb9c5d40d9737a6.png"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748053/4b38a9f3e931ab8b4edd8d4bd08beed40905b3c3.png"]
Patch 1.7 is here, and brings our final patch before Hell Let Loose: Vietnam launch its next major content drop with Update 2.0 in November.

This patch introduces weapon changes including the addition of Hell Let Loose fan favourite the M1A1 Thompson, as well as a new 30-round magazine option for the M16A1. We also are bringing significant visual and performance upgrades, Tank Shell Unloading, improvements to Boats, punishment changes and another extensive round of quality-of-life improvements and bug fixes.

We’ve also continued acting on your feedback, with changes including improved Boat spawn behaviour, more Barbed Wire for Engineers, a reduced AFK timer on Official Servers and additional controller options.

And once Patch 1.7 is in your hands, all eyes turn to Update 2.0, bringing our first new battlefield, Khe Sanh, the expansion of the US & Allied Forces with the arrival of ANZAC Forces, new weapons and much more.
Be sure to watch the latest Command Post video where our first look for Khe Sanh has been revealed.
Here’s everything arriving in Patch 1.7.
We are excited to be bringing a fan-favourite submachine gun over from Hell Let Loose to help boost the US Forces weapon pool:
The M1A1 Thompson joins the US Forces arsenal with Patch 1.7, bringing another hard-hitting close-quarters option to the battlefield and providing the US with an SMG counterpart to the NVA’s K50M.

Be sure to watch the latest command post to hear from the dev team about bringing this weapon over from Hell Let Loose into Hell Let Loose: Vietnam.
To learn more about the history of the M1A1 Thompson and its use during the Vietnam War, be sure to check out our partner's, the Royal Armouries, description below:

“The Thompson was initially developed in 1919, but was widely adopted by the US military in 1938 and saw extensive use during World War 2. The Thompson was declared obsolete in 1957, but a large number of the SMGs were kept in storage. So when military aid to South Vietnam was increased, these Thompsons were sent to be used primarily by the Army of the Republic of Vietnam (ARVN).

While the Thompson was provided in large numbers to South Vietnam, it saw limited use during the Vietnam War. With the Thompson being designed for trench warfare, it excelled at close-quarters combat, this was thanks to its relatively slow muzzle velocity and .45 caliber, meaning the Thompson hit hard at close range. However, the Thompson was also heavy, had poor penetration through the dense jungle foliage, and had complex maintenance needs, which meant it was not widely adopted by the ARVN. These issues meant it was quickly replaced by the M16A1 when it came into service.”
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748053/cdc18465de899ccffc3c6245660d1946f3df61e1.jpg"]
We are continuing to show some love to the US Force’s primary assault rifle, as the M16A1 sees another change after Patch 1.5’s balance update.
Alongside its existing 20-round magazine, the M16A1 can now be equipped with an optional 30-round magazine.
The 30-round configuration comes with 6 magazines by default, which can be increased to a maximum of 10 through the Barracks loadout system.

That additional ammunition comes with a trade-off, as the gun with a 30-round mag weighs an extra point, and each 30-round magazine costs 2 Weight, compared with 1 Weight for the existing 20-round magazine. giving players another choice when building their loadout.
Following your feedback in our recent Community Updates, we’ve made an important change to how Transport Boats behave when their driver leaves the controls.

When a player manually leaves the Driver seat, the Boat’s engine will now automatically switch off, allowing it to become available as a spawn point without another player needing to enter the vehicle first.

However, following your feedback, we’ve deliberately preserved an important piece of counterplay. If the Driver is killed while still in their seat, the engine will remain running. This means successfully eliminating an enemy Boat Driver can still prevent that Boat from immediately becoming available as a spawn point.
We’ve made several balancing changes to both factions’ boats to make them more responsive and easier to navigate through tighter waterways.
Both boats have received improvements to handling and top speed.
The US PBR now has a greater advantage in speed and acceleration to offset the NVA boat’s ability to transport Supplies.
To better reflect that additional utility, the NVA boat’s Fuel cost has increased by 50 fuel, from 200 to 250 fuel.

A familiar feature from Hell Let Loose arrives in Vietnam with Patch 1.7, as Tank crews can now unload their currently chambered shell when switching ammunition types, removing the need to fire the loaded round before changing ammunition.
Simply cycle to, or select another shell type and the current loaded round will be unloaded before the new ammunition type is automatically loaded.
This may be a small change, but for those tankers familiar to Hell Let Loose, we know you’ll be very excited to see this feature return.

Patch 1.7 introduces PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) support for PS5 Pro, helping deliver improved image clarity and visual stability.
For players on the base PS5, we’re also looking to integrate PlayStation’s recently announced QSSR technology once it becomes available for us to implement.
We’ll share more details on that integration in the future.
Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) is now supported on compatible displays for both PS5 and PS5 Pro, joining the existing VRR support on Xbox Series X|S.
VRR helps provide smoother and more consistent frame delivery by reducing visible screen tearing and judder during fluctuations in frame rate.
Alongside the introduction of FSR 4.1 in Hotfix 1.5.2, Patch 1.7 brings AMD FSR Frame Generation to supported AMD GPUs (5000 series and above).
Frame Generation creates additional frames between traditionally rendered frames to help deliver a smoother experience and increase the displayed frame rate.
The option can be enabled through the Video Settings on supported hardware.

For the best experience, we recommend using Frame Generation when your base frame rate is already around 60 FPS or above, particularly when targeting higher-refresh-rate displays otherwise latency will increase.
We’ve reviewed several areas where the current punishment system could penalise players for using intended gameplay mechanics.
Firstly, we’ve removed the 10-second punishment for choosing to Redeploy.
Redeploying is an important tactical tool for repositioning around the battlefield, and players will still need to wait for the normal deployment timer before returning to the fight.
Secondly, we’ve also changed how Commander Orders interact with team-kill punishments.

Friendlies wandering it to hot-zones is all too common after an order has been issued for the greater good of the team. Commanders will therefore no longer receive a team-kill punishment when friendly players are killed by Commander abilities such as:
Napalm
Artillery Strikes
Bombing Runs
This way Commanders won’t have to wait potentially minutes at a time to re-spawn after death.
Personal weapons and other direct actions will continue to behave as normal.
Unit names have been updated to use the NATO Phonetic Alphabet, providing period-appropriate naming across Squads:

A – Alfa, B – Bravo, C – Charlie, D – Delta, E – Echo, F – Foxtrot, G – Golf, H – Hotel, I – India, J – Juliett, K – Kilo, L – Lima, M – Mike, N – November, O – Oscar, P – Papa, Q – Quebec, R – Romeo, S – Sierra, T – Tango, U – Uniform, V – Victor, W – Whiskey, X – X-ray, Y – Yankee, Z – Zulu
Alongside the headline changes above, Patch 1.7 includes a number of additional quality-of-life improvements requested by the community:
Barracks Navigation - Removed the lengthy camera sequence when entering and leaving the Barracks, allowing you to move between front-end menus much faster.
Official Server AFK Timer - Reduced the AFK kick timer on Official Servers from 30 minutes to 10 minutes, helping free up spaces occupied by inactive players.
Vehicle Impact Thresholds - Further increased the vehicle speed required to run over and kill infantry, reducing deaths caused by slow-moving vehicles.
More Barbed Wire - Engineers can now construct 3 Barbed Wire placements, increased from 2. The team-wide limit has been adjusted to 50.
Controller Crouch/Melee Toggle - Added a new controller option allowing players to swap the Crouch and Melee inputs across all controller layouts.
Tutorials - Improved the UI so that the status of the tutorials is now more clearly labelled, so you know which tutorials have and haven’t been completed.

Patch 1.6 is now live, bringing a major audio overhaul, Unit composition changes, a rework of Engineer Buildables, significant Admin Camera improvements and much more.
Alongside these larger changes, Patch 1.6 includes another extensive round of quality-of-life improvements and bug fixes across gameplay, vehicles, UI, servers, maps and more.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748053/767770718d9b64b6f13df5d04bea72ff840e9abe.png"]

We’ve adjusted Unit composition to provide Squads with greater flexibility and help keep more players alive and in the fight.
Units can now field 2 Medics, increased from 1, while the number of available Rifleman slots has been reduced from 3 to 2.

The Engineer is an essential role on the battlefield, with their ability to build defenses for the team to fortify a position. However, we’ve seen that with the faster pace of Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, combined with the importance of supplies for maintaining spawn networks, Engineers have fewer opportunities to fortify positions than we’d like.
With Patch 1.6, we’re making a major pass on Buildables to make defensive construction more accessible, useful and worthwhile.
The biggest change is that all Level 1 Buildables are now free to place and construct.
Supplies are still required to upgrade them to higher levels, but Engineers can now establish basic defensive positions without consuming the team’s Supply reserves.
The limits per item have changed though, so you won’t be able to place quite as many per engineer:
Barbed Wire: 2 per engineer (unlimited per team)
Barricade: 2 per engineer (50 per team)
Bunker: 1 per engineer (10 per team)
Additionally the buildables themselves are more useful, redesigned to provide better protection for superior cover, with additional elements added to make them harder to scale or navigate.

Barbed Wire is now unique to each faction, with layouts that have different pass through sections. Bleed damage is still applied so players must take this into consideration if they risk pushing through.

We know the Admin Camera plays an important role for competitive events, casting and community broadcasts. Following feedback from those using it, Patch 1.6 includes a substantial round of improvements to make spectating matches smoother and more reliable.
Camera shake is now applied when observing another user firing their weapon from the first person perspective
Scoped weapons and equipment, alongside deployed Machine Guns, are now displayed from the correct point of view
Locking your view onto the Mortars, AA guns & boats no longer places the camera underground.
Updated the camera positions for both factions’ boats.
The Cycle Camera Adjust overlay now reflects the correct mouse button bindings
The first equip of the M72 of an observed player in first person perspective now plays the equip animation correctly
Players are now returned to the first person perspective of the player being watched when they leave a vehicle
Conflicting keybindings in the admin camera have been resolved
When returning to gameplay after disabling the HUD in the admin camera, the HUD appears as expected
The button for exiting the Admin Camera has been renamed to “Leave Admin Camera"
If you’d like to see admin camera in action, be sure to check out some of our Content Corp such as SmithersCast and DasAltberg.
Commander Order overlays could previously remain on the Tactical Map long after an ability had begun, creating unnecessary clutter.
In Patch 1.6, the radial timer for each Commander Order is now individually timed to complete when the effect begins, such as when the first bomb is released during a Bombing Run.
This should keep the Tactical Map clearer and make it easier for Commanders to see the impact of their Orders.

notes.title: Important Note for PC Players: Shader Caching & Video Settings

items.text: Following each update, shaders will be cached when you first launch the game. Please allow this process, and the initial loading screens, to fully complete before continuing.
Continuing while shader caching is still taking place may result in the game crashing.
We’re looking at ways to improve how shader caching is handled in future updates to make this initial experience smoother, and we’ll share more details once those improvements are confirmed.

We also recommend that all PC players using either AMD or NVIDIA GPUs reset their Video Settings to default following the update. This will allow the game to correctly recalibrate your settings following the introduction of AMD FSR 4.1.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748053/8dce121bad01cf8a93a8e4d8557102d8fc09bebd.png"]
AMD FSR 4.1 support is now available for players using AMD Radeon RX 7000 Series GPUs and above.
AMD has also confirmed plans to back-port FSR 4.1 support to the Radeon RX 6000 Series in 2027.
FSR 4.1 uses machine learning to reconstruct higher-quality visuals from lower-resolution frames, helping improve performance while maintaining image quality.
Players can choose between several FSR 4.1 quality modes depending on whether they would prefer to prioritise image quality or performance:
Native AA - Provides image quality superior to native rendering, with a modest performance cost.
Quality - Provides image quality equal or superior to native rendering, alongside a significant performance gain.
Balanced - Offers a balance between image quality and improved performance.
Performance - Provides image quality similar to native rendering, with a larger performance gain.
Ultra Performance - Provides the highest performance gain while maintaining image quality representative of native rendering.
We identified several edge cases that could cause other players to become silently muted, resulting in some players being unable to hear one another.
Hotfix 1.5.2 introduces additional safeguards designed to reduce the likelihood of this occurring and improve the overall reliability of player communications.
We’ll continue monitoring VOIP reports following the hotfix.
Fixed an issue where signing out of Epic Online Services (EOS) could cause game settings to reset after signing back in.
Your game settings should now be retained when signing in and out of EOS.
We’ve made further improvements to how the game manages memory during gameplay.

These changes reduce the amount of data being held in memory, helping free up additional VRAM. This should provide performance improvements, particularly for players using GPUs with lower amounts of available VRAM.
We’ve made a series of improvements to Iris, the replication system used to communicate game state between the server and players.

Over longer periods of server activity, replication issues could contribute to what we refer to as server degradation, where elements such as spawn points, HQs, vehicles, ladders and other objects could stop behaving or appearing correctly.
Hotfix 1.5.2 introduces several fixes designed to reduce instances of this behaviour and improve server reliability over longer sessions.
We’ll continue monitoring reports following the update to assess the impact of these changes.
A number of further stability improvements have been introduced with Hotfix 1.5.2.
This includes a fix for a potential memory corruption issue that could result in a crash, alongside fixes for several VFX-related issues involving flares.
We’ll continue reviewing incoming crash data and addressing further stability issues as they are identified.
We identified a rare issue on PS5 that could result in players losing their save data.
Additional safeguards have now been introduced to further protect against this occurring.
Fixed an issue where certain trees could incorrectly display their distant 2D impostor versions when close to the player.
These assets will now correctly transition to their full 3D models at the intended distance, improving visual quality and reducing noticeable tree pop-in.
Patch 1.6 is coming next, and we’ll be sharing more details on what’s included very soon, so keep an eye on our channels for the full breakdown.
As always, thank you for continuing to share your reports and feedback. We’ll continue monitoring the impact of Hotfix 1.5.2 as we work towards Patch 1.6.

Update 1.5 is almost here, bringing our first major content drop since the launch of Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, alongside a host of bug fixes and issue resolutions.
Take to the skies in the officially licensed Bell UH-1 Iroquois ‘Huey’, get hands-on with the brand-new M14 and Type 56 SKS, and experience our first balancing pass on the launch weapon arsenal.

Alongside the new content, Update 1.5 brings further improvements to Helicopter gameplay, Commander Orders, spawning, the Tactical Map and more, with 100+ fixes and quality-of-life improvements across the game.
Whether you’re taking the Huey into battle, trying out the latest additions to your loadout or returning to the front lines to see what’s changed, there’s plenty to get your hands on in Update 1.5.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748053/925c6d6efbd1ea1b8076cd35d1b6bae1e6eb9ae6.png"]

The Bell UH-1 Iroquois (commonly nicknamed the ‘Huey’) is a utility military helicopter designed and produced by the American aerospace company Bell Helicopter. It is the first member of the prolific 'Huey' family, as well as the first turbine-powered helicopter in service with the United States military.
The officially licensed Huey replaces the existing fictional helicopter model and arrives with a number of gameplay improvements and balancing changes.
HUD Icons - New HUD icons for pilots and co-pilots to communicate the status of Supply Drops, Spawning, Auto Levelling, the Cockpit Radio & Repairs/Resupply.

M60 Ammunition - Upgraded the ammunition type for M61 AP rounds so they can now damage boats and tunnels, with an increased number of tracer rounds to make it easier to see where you’re shooting. The ammo capacity has also been increased from 400 to 500 rounds.
Cockpit Alarm - The helicopter cockpit audio alarm plays to alert you when your hull health is low.

Death Sequence & Destruction - When the Helicopter is destroyed, occupants no longer die instantly. Instead, the aircraft will crash to the ground before being destroyed, with improved explosion VFX and death-state transitions.
Rotor Blades - Rotor blades can no longer destroy friendly or enemy structures, while the tail rotor can now damage infantry.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748053/9cd3e809e29c11d66a42cdc12cbacc952a679cae.jpg"]

The UH-1 Huey features a built-in radio that can be toggled by the Co-Pilot. Music will be heard by everyone inside the Helicopter, as well as nearby players from either faction as the Huey travels across the battlefield.
Players who would prefer not to hear the music, including content creators and streamers, can disable Helicopter music within the Audio Settings.
Be sure to check out the Vietnam Radio Station Playlist on Spotify to get yourself ready for take off. Hell Let Loose: Vietnam Radio Station
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748053/b8b5bb09aae3483c06fe5615ec9dc962e9146ac7.jpg"]
As a thank you to everyone who has joined us since launch, a new US Pilot Uniform will be arriving in your Barracks with Update 1.5.
The uniform will be available free to all players who log in during Update 1.5, before becoming available for purchase at a later date.
Be sure to jump in and claim it while it’s available, ready to take to the skies in your new Huey!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748053/c2cde2b58851e810bde26b52502a6eb0b06589c1.jpg"]
The M14 rifle saw combat in Vietnam as early as 1961, as a replacement for the M1 Garand. The M14 is a large and heavy rifle that uses 7.62 x 51mm rounds, giving it a lot of stopping power.
However, because the weapon was extremely difficult to handle in fully automatic mode, and was later replaced with a version that had the selector shaft locked to only allow semi-auto fire.
This semi-automatic configuration is the version arriving in Hell Let Loose: Vietnam as part of Update 1.5.
Semi-Automatic Rifle using 7.62 x 51 mm rounds
20-round magazine capacity, with a default of 4 magazines that are upgradeable to 8 (2 weight per magazine).
Available to the following roles at level 3: Squad Leader, Rifleman, Specialist & Engineer.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748053/cfad5895ec0770d8c7cc992b37f31a935cb51a45.jpg"]

The SKS was the standard infantry rifle early in the Vietnam war before being swapped out by the Type 56 AK. The SKS is fitted with a 10-round non-detachable internal magazine, to load the SKS, the bolt was locked open, and a 10-round charger clip was used to push the rounds into the magazine.
Semi-Automatic Rifle using 7.62 x 39mm rounds
10-round internal magazine capacity, with a default of 6 Clips that are upgradeable to 12 (1 weight per Clip).
Available to the following roles at level 3: Squad Leader, Rifleman, Specialist & Engineer.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748053/4a0b834742ae8621e7b79139f372dc5cd3b4f657.jpg"]
With Update 1.5, we’re making our first balancing pass on some of the weapons available at launch.
As part of this, we’ve increased the M16’s default ammunition from 4 to 6 magazines, bringing its starting ammunition capacity in line with the Type 56 AK.
Players can also now increase the M16’s magazine allowance to a maximum of 10 magazines through the loadout system in the Barracks, compared with a maximum of 7 magazines for the Type 56 AK.
Expect to see more weapon balancing coming in future updates.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748053/d17fd649fae53b286c318f8b0741f72bfd126725.jpg"]

This update is aiming to resolve two of the major community-reported issues we’ve been tracking; the first being distorted, robotic voices in Proximity Chat, and the second is persistent Recon Plane and Flare markers.

Patch 1.4 also introduces DLSS 4.5 support, with additional Frame Generation options, adds further protection against Career Level resets, and brings improvements to Tunnels, the Tactical Map, spawning, controls and more.
Thank you as always for continuing to share your reports and feedback with us. Here are some of the key improvements included in Patch 1.4:

We know that this has been one of the most frequently reported issues since launch and follows the improvements introduced in Patch 1.3 while we continued investigating the underlying cause.

Patch 1.3 is now live for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, bringing another round of fixes, improvements and balancing changes based on the issues and feedback you’ve been sharing with us.

This patch includes changes to NVA Tunnel balancing, improvements to Armor gear shifting, an important workaround targeting stability issues affecting players using AMD hardware, further improvements to console image quality, and a range of fixes for community server owners.
Alongside these headline changes, Patch 1.3 includes further improvements across gameplay, vehicles, weapons, UI and controls, audio, tutorials, VOIP, maps and more.
Thank you for continuing to share your reports and feedback with us. Here are some of the key improvements included in Patch 1.3:
We’re making further adjustments to NVA Tunnels based on gameplay data and community feedback.
The Tunnel placement cooldown has been doubled from 5 minutes to 10 minutes, slowing the rate at which the NVA can place and replace their Tunnel network.
Players will also no longer be able to travel to a Tunnel destination while it is considered ‘hot’, bringing this behaviour in line with Garrisons.

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748053/84cb84ca9b2d9e1474f911cef0f3c112426d5758.png"]

[p align="start"]First of all, a huge thank you to the hundreds of thousands of players who joined us over the course of last weekend's Crossplay Playtest. It was fantastic to see so many players across Steam, PlayStation and XBOX taking to the battlefield together, as well as all the incredible clips, screenshots and feedback shared by the community.
[p align="start"]With launch on 13 August fast approaching, we cannot wait for you to experience the full game, including all of the maps that weren't available during the playtest.

[p align="start"]Since the playtest concluded, the team has been reviewing thousands of responses to the feedback survey, alongside reports and discussions across Discord, Reddit, Steam and our other community channels. This feedback has been invaluable in helping us prioritise the areas that matter most ahead of launch, while reinforcing and shaping the improvements we had already planned for release.

[p align="start"]Today, we want to share what we've been working on since the Crossplay Playtest, including improvements that weren't ready in time for the playtest, the changes coming at launch, and what we'll continue refining after release.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748053/65ff1c498a52118fd3e1bfd7ed4de3e278f5fc77.jpg"]

notes.title: What we’re doing to prepare for launch

items.text: Alongside continued bug fixing, optimisation and polish, the team has been focused on addressing feedback from the recent playtest. While we'll continue improving the game after launch through regular updates, here are some of the key improvements players can expect on day one:
The team has made significant progress in addressing the known VOIP issues encountered during the playtest.
Players should no longer experience the robotic voice effect in Command Chat or Squad Chat. While the issue can still occur in Proximity Chat, it should happen much less frequently.

The remaining Proximity Chat issue requires an update to the Epic Online Services (EOS) voice chat system. As soon as a fix is made available by Epic, we'll work to integrate it into the game as quickly as possible.

The team has reviewed all audio feedback from the playtest and has made a wide range of improvements ahead of launch. Audio will continue to be refined through future patches and updates, but players can expect the following changes at release:
Adjustments to helicopter SFX, including changes over distance.
Reduction in volume of front end music
Increased readability in the sonic soundscape to improve player navigation in the battlefield, including:
Pings - Raised within the mix to support improvements with spatial audio
Foliage - Increased in volume to support improvements with spatial audio
All Weapons - Improved pin-pointing and adjustments to support improvements with spatial audio
Improvements to headshot and hit confirmation sounds.
Decrease in volume to water wading.
Underwater swimming audio bug resolved.
Adjustments and improvements to character foley.
Commander abilities and explosions have received further adjustments and improvements.
All vehicles and vehicle types have had an audio balancing pass.
Wider improvements and changes made within the mix.
Based on playtest feedback, we've made several adjustments to improve early player progression and better support the new weighted loadout system:
Faster player progression through earlier role levels
Improved starting weight for selected roles
Reduced the weight of selected weapons to make them available earlier in progression
We have been continually reviewing player feedback alongside gameplay analytics to ensure the battlefield remains as balanced as possible.

As players continue to develop new tactics and strategies with both US Helicopters and NVA Tunnels, we'll continue to monitor their performance after launch and make balance adjustments where necessary.

Following the Crossplay Playtest, we've already identified several changes we'd like to make to the tunnel system, with a particular focus on tunnel travel speed and the Emergency Tunnel Commander ability.

notes.title: For launch, we're planning the following changes

items.text: Reduce the maximum tunnel connection limit from 5 to 4
Reduce tunnel travel speed to make rapid redeployment less effective

Remove the Emergency Tunnel Commander ability. We believe this mechanic requires a more comprehensive redesign before it returns to the game, and we'll continue exploring how it could be implemented in the future.
As always, we'll continue monitoring feedback and gameplay data after launch and make further balance adjustments where needed.

The team are continuing work investigating the AMD GPU crashes experienced by some users during the playtest. While most issues appear to be caused by known AMD Windows driver issues outside our control, we have identified some fixes that may lessen crashes and improve stability overall for AMD users.

Based on findings and feedback from the playtest, we’ve been investigating shadows and foliage on console platforms with the goal of reducing issues with flickering and popping during gameplay. While this will remain a balance between visual fidelity and performance, we’re continuing to work hard to find the right balance ahead of launch.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748053/2ff537f3250807b942cb5132904be0168a3bb6f0.jpg"]

We know there are still plenty of features, improvements and fixes that both the community and the team want to see added after launch. Alongside regular patches to address bugs and player feedback, we'll also be bringing new content to Hell Let Loose: Vietnam in future updates.
If you're interested in what lies beyond launch, keep an eye out for Part 2 of our Developer Q&A.

Tomorrow, 31 July, we will be releasing Part 2 of the Developer Q&A where the team will be going behind the scenes to explore how the team has developed a new Hell Let Loose experience, the ideas that were tested along the way, and how the Vietnam and World War II development teams work together, and also a look toward the future of the game, talking about the team’s long-term ambitions for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam.

notes.title: Cross-Platform Play in Hell Let Loose: Vietnam

items.text: With the Open Beta coming soon, and it being available on multiple platforms, we wanted to reopen the conversation around cross-platform play.
We know that the Hell Let Loose community plays across many different platforms, and cross-platform play is something the community cares a lot about.
Some players prefer to keep console and PC separate, while others want the option to play with friends on different platforms.
As we have developed Hell Let Loose: Vietnam, we wanted to revisit this topic and find a more flexible approach for all players and server owners.
On launch cross-platform play will be a feature in Hell Let Loose: Vietnam.
The way this will operate is that in-game servers will be clearly tagged as cross-platform play, PC only, or console only, allowing players to choose the experience that suits them.

Server owners will now also have the ability to enable cross-platform play and decide which platforms are allowed on their server. This provides greater control and flexibility, without forcing cross-platform play on all players.
We hope that this will be a welcome feature and people are excited for Hell Let Loose: Vietnam’s cross-platform play functionality.
